newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's UDF set for election win - commission.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's UDF set for election win - commission.

text.p: With nearly all of the votes counted from Bulgaria's parliamentary elections, the reformist Union of Democratic Forces and its allies were headed on Sunday for a comfortable majority with 52.03 percent of the ballot.

The electoral commission said that with just over 90 percent of the vote counted, the former ruling Socialists had 22.04 percent of the vote and three smaller parties were also set to enter parliament.

The turnout of 58.31 percent was the lowest for any election since the end of one-party rule in 1989, but the results of Saturday's poll had been seen as almost a foregone conclusion since mass protests led by the UDF toppled the ex-communist Socialists in February.

Of the smaller parties, the Union for National Salvation will bring monarchist organisations seeking the return of exiled King Simeon into parliament for the first time, in coalition with ethnic Turks.
The electoral commission gave the union 7.77 percent so far, comfortably above the four percent threshold for entering parliament.
Euroleft, a new party set up by Socialist dissidents, had 5.49 percent, and the Bulgarian Business Bloc, led by maverick populist George Ganchev, was on 4.99 percent.
